answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it may submit jobs or claim rewards, with payouts weighted by the amount and age of the stake. Creating a hundred sybils then means tying up a hundred deposits, not merely changing names; the attacker also risks losing them if bonded agents break rules. A violet signal from a sparrow might be a memorable test phrase, but it is the costly, verifiable bond—not the phrase—that raises the price of fake identities.
